quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal when turning from this lane.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. If you are turning in that direction, get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before you turn.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to know where traffic behind you is located.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is coming ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is coming ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers to watch for a side road that crosses ahead.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to control the bicycle completely.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and may change direction without warning. Children and bicycles are small and easy to miss, so stay alert.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines mean any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Spots in your vision when you get tired.
Areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check blind spots. These are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: When passing another car, when do you have enough space to return to the driving lane?

options.text: If the other driver signals for you to move back.
If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to the driving lane, make sure there is a safe distance between your vehicle and the car you passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Make extra space for drivers to merge safely.
Traffic is entering from another road. Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Make extra space for drivers to merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will merge into your lane. Check your side and rearview mirrors. If possible, move to another lane to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
It is not safe to pass.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot legally pass in that area. These zones are in places where visibility is limited and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Expect them to drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks with flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. They stop whether or not a train is coming. You should be ready to stop too.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is coming ahead.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow down to the posted freeway speed limit.
Wait until you enter the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Cannot be seen by the truck driver or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths of space between their vehicle and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be seen by the truck driver or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are too close to the truck. In these areas, the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Cars in "No zones" have a much higher risk of crashing.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. The more alcohol you drink, the worse your judgment and driving skills become. You will have trouble judging distance, speed, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers can cross it to change lanes. A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass if you are next to the broken line. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop right away in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right edge of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or siren, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. You must always give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol and its harmful effects from your body.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the road shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
A divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions right ahead. This sign tells you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: When a person crossing the street uses a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a person using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Wait until they are well away from your vehicle. Always let blind pedestrians cross first.

questions.question: A bad suspension system can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and makes rides smooth. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use the whole lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share the same lane. If you return to the right lane too soon, the motorcycle rider may have to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look both left and right for vehicles and pedestrians before entering. Look left a second time because vehicles from the left will be closer to you. Check across the entire intersection to make sure it is clear before you go.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights and sirens. Move to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering an interstate. Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic already on the highway, then merge smoothly when it is safe.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety, but never faster. Slow down for curves, hills with limited view, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected changes. Drive with great care to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Equally between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Equally between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you have oncoming vehicles on your left and parked vehicles on your right, steer down the middle. Balance your position between both sides.

questions.question: How can you help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance. This helps the driver behind you know what you are doing and maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It can be hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may seem slower than they really are. Only pass when you are sure you can safely change lanes. If you are not sure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass the other car.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not count on the other driver to make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not count on the other driver to make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even when you signal, do not assume that other drivers will give you the right-of-way or make space for you.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane, no matter what other lights are showing. Before you turn, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection go first.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, release the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids to the left, steer left. This helps straighten out your car.

questions.question: You arrive at a four-way stop at the same time as the driver on your left. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You.
Whoever is signaling a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You.
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or other property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle or property.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. If police find any trace of alcohol, you will face tough penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a winding road ahead. Slow down when you see this sign.
